subject: Pathology
summary: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) is a life‑threatening microangiopathy caused by severe ADAMTS13 deficiency, leading to ultra‑large VWF multimers, platelet‑rich microthrombi, MAHA, and organ dysfunction.

sections.p: TTP is a thrombotic microangiopathy defined by ADAMTS13 activity <10% with clinical pentad of MAHA, severe thrombocytopenia, neurologic change, renal impairment, and fever.
b: Diagnose by peripheral smear (schistocytes) and ADADMT13 assay if available
Use PLASMIC score to estimate likelihood before ADAMTS13 result

t.b: Does the patient have fragmented red cells? → Presence of schistocytes confirms microangiopathic hemolysis.
Is activity <10%? → Strongly supports TTP; if unavailable, rely on PLASMIC score.
What is the pre‑test probability? → Score ≥6 indicates high risk, prompting urgent plasma exchange.

sections.p: Severity is gauged by organ involvement and PLASMIC score; no formal stage, but high‑risk patients need immediate plasma exchange and ICU care.
b: Neurologic deficits or rising creatinine signal severe disease
Platelet count <30 × 10⁹/L and LDH >2× upper limit suggest high burden

sections.p: Most TTP is acquired, immune‑mediated anti‑ADAMTS13 antibodies; secondary causes include infections, drugs, pregnancy, and autoimmune diseases.
b: Autoimmune anti‑ADAMTS13 antibodies (most common)
HIV, hepatitis B, malaria, TB – relevant in low‑resource settings
Drugs: quinine, ticlopidine, clopidogrel, cyclosporine
Pregnancy/post‑partum period

sections.p: Patients develop sudden fatigue, pallor, petechiae, bruising, confusion or seizures, and may have mild renal dysfunction or fever.
b: Fatigue, dyspnea from anemia
Petechiae, mucosal bleeding from thrombocytopenia
Altered mental status, seizures, headache
Creatinine rise or oliguria (often mild)

sections.p: Lab work focuses on hemolysis, platelet count, renal function, and ADAMTS13 activity; imaging only if neurologic signs demand.
b: CBC, peripheral smear, LDH, bilirubin, haptoglobin
Renal panel, urinalysis for hematuria
ADAMTS13 activity, inhibitor assay

t.b: Is there anemia with schistocytes and low platelets? → Confirms MAHA and thrombocytopenia.
Are they markedly elevated? → Indicates ongoing hemolysis.
Is renal function impaired? → Guides severity and need for dialysis.
Is activity <10%? → Confirms TTP; if unavailable, treat based on clinical score.

sections.p: Rapid neurologic decline, refractory hypertension, or worsening renal failure signal imminent organ loss; untreated TTP can be fatal.
b: Severe seizures or coma
Sudden rise in creatinine >2 mg/dL
Uncontrolled hypertension with end‑organ signs

sections.p: Urgent plasma exchange replaces deficient ADAMTS13 and removes antibodies; immunosuppression with steroids and rituximab curtails antibody production.
b: Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) daily until platelet count >150 × 10⁹/L
High‑dose methylprednisolone → suppresses auto‑antibody formation
Rituximab (anti‑CD20) for refractory or relapsing disease
Avoid platelet transfusion unless life‑threatening bleeding

sections.p: Monitor platelet count, LDH, and neurologic status daily; after remission, schedule ADAMTS13 activity checks and educate on trigger avoidance.
b: Weekly labs until stable, then monthly for 6 months
Vaccinate against infections that may precipitate relapse (e.g., influenza)
Counsel on avoiding quinine‑containing drinks and certain herbal remedies

sections.p: Conditions sharing MAHA and thrombocytopenia can mislead clinicians.
b: Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS) – more renal, often diarrheal prodrome
Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) – abnormal PT/aPTT, fibrinogen low
Severe sepsis with consumptive coagulopathy

sections.p: Certain labs may appear normal early, delaying treatment.
b: ADAMTS13 may be unavailable or delayed; rely on PLASMIC score
PT/aPTT often normal in TTP, so normal coagulation does not exclude disease
Creatinine may be only mildly raised despite severe microthrombi

whenToSeekHelp: Rapid rise in creatinine or oliguria

faq.q: Why are platelet transfusions usually avoided in TTP?
faq.a: They add substrate for microthrombi, worsening organ ischemia.

faq.q: What is the PLASMIC score used for?
faq.a: To estimate the probability of severe ADAMTS13 deficiency before lab confirmation.
Yes; pregnancy‑associated TTP is an immune form that requires plasma exchange and steroids.

exam: Explain how ADAMTS13 deficiency leads to the clinical pentad of TTP.
Describe the steps you would take to diagnose TTP when ADAMTS13 testing is not immediately available.
List the first‑line therapies for TTP and the rationale for avoiding platelet transfusion.
